source_status.exact_result: Unverified author proof draft: for every complete nontrivially valued K, every separable quadratic E/K, and every good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional K-analytic space (n >= 1), including singular and nonreduced structures, the ordinary CLD zero-Hessian equation of every continuous finite h automatically ascends to X_E and is equivalent there to the ground-field equation. This includes Q2(sqrt2)/Q2 without a residue-separating unit and iterates through finite quadratic towers. Fixed-support differentiated total-variation approximation of invariant compact ordinary (n-1,n-1) tests is proved, rather than exact ramified ordinary form descent.
concrete_gaps: Original P06.2 classical recognition on arbitrary good separated strict boundaryless spaces and ordinary two-sign current-positive regularization remain unproved; no original strict analytic counterexample is claimed.
Scalar-current ascent through general finite separable extensions outside finite quadratic towers, completed infinite algebraic extensions and transcendental analytic extensions remains unproved.
Universal classical curve-test quantifiers over all analytic extensions remain untreated; the new scalar gate alone does not supply recognition.
Exact invariant ordinary smooth form descent and preservation of positive test cones are not claimed; positive-current ascent and ordinary harmonic approximation remain separate.
The draft has a fallible author self-audit and finite build/diagnostic evidence only, with no independent mathematical verification or inherited parent verdict.

source_clarification.before:
CLD Corollary 15.2.9: if $F$
   is a closed subset countable at infinity (in particular compact) of
   such a space and $(U_i)$ is an ordinary open cover of $F$, there are
   nonnegative ordinary smooth functions $\chi_i$, locally finite,
   compactly supported in their respective $U_i$, with
   $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ near $F$. Only finite covers of compact sets are
   used here.
source_clarification.after: For a compact subset $F$ and a finite ordinary open cover $(U_i)$ of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. This compact specialization follows from CLD Corollary 15.2.5 and ordinary smooth functional calculus. For each $x\in F$, apply 15.2.5 with $\{x\}\subset U_i$ to obtain a smooth function equal to one near $x$ and compactly supported in $U_i$. Compose with a nonnegative smooth real function equal to zero near zero and equal to one near one, obtaining a nonnegative bump with the same support containment. Compactness selects finitely many such bumps; group them by cover index into $\psi_i$, and put $s=\sum_i\psi_i$. Then $s>0$ near $F$. Apply 15.2.5 again to compact $F$ inside the open $\{s>0\}$, and the same nonnegative composition, to obtain $\chi$ compactly supported there and equal to one near $F$. Set $\theta_i=\chi\psi_i/s$ on that open and extend by zero. Smoothness follows since the support of $\chi$ lies compactly inside the open. Each $\theta_i$ has compact support inside $U_i$ and their sum is $\chi$. No arbitrary countable-at-infinity, fixed-cover-index compact-support assertion is used. Only this compact-set, finite-cover version is needed.

result.report:
The stated quadratic transport theorem and its fixed-support differentiated total-variation approximation are established. This verdict concerns the supplied partial theorem; original P06.2, classical recognition, and two-sign regularization remain open.

I checked the relevant statements and proof bodies in the specified [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) and [GR v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13548v2). The external dependencies are recorded below. Passage quotations are short textual or mathematical anchors to those statements; the audit used their full hypotheses and surrounding proofs.

The finite-tensor argument works with the unreduced algebra. Bounded coordinate maps on the finite-dimensional extension identify the completed tensor with A⊕Aa. Taking invariants is a kernel calculation over K, so B^σ=A also in characteristic two. Invariant units descend together with their inverses. Spectral surjectivity justifies the unit criterion without removing nilpotents. Over every analytic point, the separable quadratic polynomial gives one field factor or two field factors; uniqueness of an extending absolute value follows by comparing equivalent norms on powers. The involution is transitive on these factors. Thus the singleton/two-point fibre division exhausts all analytic points.

Compactness and full-fibre shrinking are valid. A compact downstairs set has compact inverse image using finitely many affinoid neighbourhood interiors. Inside an affinoid neighbourhood, the image of the compact complement of a full-fibre open is closed and avoids the base point. A smaller strict affinoid neighbourhood therefore retains all finitely many required inequalities. This establishes the shrinkings used for units, zero coefficients, normalized units, pair products, and cancellation differences; it does not presume a covering map.

The ambient hypotheses are retained. Goodness follows from inverse images of affinoid interiors, strictness from strict presentations, separatedness from the diagonal, and boundarylessness from the cited boundary inclusion. Purity is checked component by component, rather than inferred from equality of total dimensions. Each minimal component downstairs has dimension n by a point whose kernel is its minimal prime. Separability makes (A/J)⊗E reduced, and its embedding into the finite product of generic field factors identifies every upstairs minimal prime as lying over a downstairs minimal prime. The supplied lying-over, going-up, and incomparability argument proves dimension equality for the resulting finite integral domain injections. Consequently every upstairs minimal component has dimension n. The reduction in this calculation is confined to dimension: integration still uses the actual fibre-algebra lengths.

Finite restriction from E to K supplies the legitimate category for the involution. More explicitly, an E-Tate algebra is finite over the corresponding K-Tate algebra by the same bounded-coordinate argument, and its quotient is K-affinoid by the finite-algebra result. Rational localizations use the same elements and inequalities. Common rational neighbourhoods, unit germs, compact moment images, and the nullity criterion identify the ordinary form sheaves and their differentials on the common carrier. The bounded coefficient involution then glues to a K-analytic automorphism there.

The ramified normalization is correct for arbitrary separable quadratic E/K. When v(x)=0, the retained strict inequalities give t_f=t_σf=t_u on the neighbourhood. When v(x)≠0, division uses only the retained unit v and the nonzero constant c. The identity F+σF=1 gives the actual three-ray moment image and δ_f²=(max(S_f,0))² at every analytic point. Neither a residue-separating unit nor a lower bound for |c| is required. Characteristic two causes no failure.

The smoothing bounds are sufficient in the differentiated topology. The first derivative of q is Lipschitz and continuous, so its weak second derivative has no atom. The stated zeroth, first, and second derivative estimates follow from convolution. On a cell with nonconstant S, the second derivative discrepancy is confined to |S|≤ε. On a cell where S is constant, its tangential derivatives vanish; in particular an entire top cell in the fold produces no second derivative discrepancy. Polarization correctly treats every δ_iδ_j, including pair products whose coefficient vanishes.

The total-variation argument controls measures on the carrier. The bideterminant contraction estimate compares absolute coefficient contractions against the positive ζ measure on the supporting skeleton, before any signed pushforward. Thus cancellation between fibres cannot conceal error. Standard canonical calibration gives finite constant positive densities after a fixed cell refinement, with the unreduced finite-flat degrees included. Fubini gives strip mass O(ε) for each nonconstant affine S. Lower-dimensional skeleton faces and hyperplane sections of nonconstant top cells have zero top measure. Constant-fold top cells and any remaining singular or conductor contributions are covered by the same tangential calculation and actual calibration; no singular locus is discarded wholesale.

The orbital identities establish ordinary form equalities. U dV−V dU vanishes on every ray, including the vertex, and hence on every compact actual moment image. CLD nullity then applies to its ordinary moment presentation. Expanding this identity for both conjugates gives exactly the factor two and signs in (18). If e_ij(x)=0, the retained strict inequalities give equal conjugate logarithms and δ_i=δ_j; if an original v_i(x)=0, δ_i=0. These cases genuinely make the orbital expression zero without dividing by a vanishing quantity.

The derivative cancellations in Sections 6.2–6.3 are valid. The coefficients of O are affine, so d'd''O=0. Consequently d'd''L_ε=0 exactly, and every P_ε is closed for both differentials. The corresponding targets satisfy the same identities. Only the bounded second derivative family of the fold smoothing enters the product estimates; third and fourth derivatives do not enter. Counting anti-invariant scalar and differential symbols proves generation of every invariant polynomial superform, including pure-prime alternating terms and ordered mixed terms. Leibniz then yields (23) for the complete differentiated family, also with a fixed ordinary cutoff.

Every compact ordinary test is covered by Section 7. At singleton fibres, ordinary moment representation, Euclidean extension, and real averaging produce the invariant smooth coefficient superform. The Gaussian/Taylor construction supplies coefficient C² polynomial approximation on a fixed swap-stable box. This C² approximation is used before the fold approximation and is not substituted for differentiated convergence at the fold. At two-point fibres, disjoint conjugate neighbourhoods and the structural sheaf glue invariant units; their invariant inverses make them actual downstairs units, giving exact local descent.

The revised cutoff construction is sound. CLD 15.2.5 applies because the space is good and Hausdorff. Finitely many bumps cover the compact F; grouping gives ψ_i, and a further compact bump χ inside {s>0} makes θ_i=χψ_i/s smooth with compact support inside U_i. Their sum is one near F. The proof uses this compact finite-cover statement only. Extension by zero is smooth because each product vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point outside its closed compact support. The finitely many moment domains and cutoff descriptions are fixed. Choosing ε_j after each polynomial P_j gives differentiated total-variation convergence with support in one compact π⁻¹(D), without any uniform estimate in polynomial degree. Boundedness of h∘π there proves the required pairing convergence.

Averaging and scalar projection have the correct, distinct normalizations. On the restricted K-carrier the involution is an analytic isomorphism of calibrated degree one. The same-carrier calibration is twice the E-calibration, and cancelling this factor proves invariance of E-measure pairings. Conversely, scalar projection satisfies the calibration pushforward identity with no extension-degree factor. Its proof sums actual fibre-algebra degrees, retaining lengths. Hence (30) is valid for differentiated ordinary tests and continuous multipliers. Averaging an arbitrary upstairs test, applying the established fixed-support approximation, and using (30) proves genuine forward ascent. Testing pulled-back downstairs forms proves the reverse implication. Ordinary opens retain the hypotheses, and the component and category checks justify each stage of a finite quadratic tower.

The Q₂(√2) calculation is correct: irreducibility follows from valuation parity, and a unit x+y√2 has v₂(x)=0 and v₂(y)≥0 when y≠0. Its conjugate difference therefore has absolute value at most 2^(-3/2), so the earlier residue-separating condition is unavailable. The proof nevertheless applies.

Harmless wording correction: Section 6.1 should say “Let F, G, e be analytic units with G=F+e.” No substantial repair of the supplied transport argument is required. Builds, finite diagnostics, parent verdicts, and listed local artifacts were not used as mathematical assumptions.

passages.statement: CLD 11.1.1–2: For a complete non-Archimedean field K, the spectrum of a K-affinoid algebra A is compact Hausdorff, A is noetherian, every ideal of A is closed, and the map M(A)→Spec(A) is surjective.

CLD 11.1.5–7: In an affinoid space, every point has rational affinoid neighbourhoods contained in any prescribed ordinary open neighbourhood. Every point of a good analytic space has an affinoid neighbourhood basis, and every ordinary open subset is an analytic domain.
CLD 11.7.6–7: Over a complete nontrivially valued field K, every point of a good strictly K-analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood.

CLD 11.1.9: Affinoid fibre products are computed by completed tensor products; for every complete analytic extension L/K, M(A)_L=M(A completed-tensor_K L), and the scalar projection X_L→X is surjective.
CLD 11.4.4: If A is K-affinoid and B is a finite A-algebra with a Banach norm equivalent to the quotient norm from a finite A-module presentation, then B is K-affinoid.

CLD 11.2.2–3: Analytically separated spaces are Hausdorff. Strict affinoid analytic dimension equals Krull dimension, scalar extension preserves analytic dimension, and analytic domains preserve local analytic dimension. For an affinoid X with minimal-prime components X_i, dim_x(X)=sup_{i:x∈X_i}dim(X_i).
GR 2.11(3)–(5′): For an analytic morphism Y→Z and every complete analytic extension L/K, ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊆π⁻¹(∂(Y/Z)). An ordinary open analytic subspace of a boundaryless analytic space is boundaryless.

passages.statement: CLD Proposition 15.1.1(b): On a topologically separated analytic space, every ordinary (p,q)-form has an ordinary open cover on whose members it is the pullback, by a unit moment, of a coefficient (p,q)-form on a paralinéaire set containing the moment image.

CLD Lemma 1.9.4 and 3.3.3: If a paralinéaire subset P of a finite-dimensional affine space is closed in an ambient open U, every smooth coefficient (p,q)-form on P extends to U; a coefficient form used in a G-tropical chart admits such an ambient-open representation.

CLD 6.2.1–2, 3.3.11–12, and 3.4.6: Ordinary smooth forms are G-form sections having tropical descriptions on ordinary neighbourhoods. They form an ordinary sheaf stable under wedge, J, d′, and d″; functorial pullbacks commute with these operations. Smooth (0,0)-forms identify injectively with their numerical functions.

CLD Propositions 3.4.1 and 3.4.4: For a G-tropical chart f:X→V and a coefficient form η on a paralinéaire set containing f(X), its pullback is zero in the G-form sheaf if and only if η restricts to zero on f(W) for every compact domain W⊆X. For compact X, the corresponding presheaf pullback is zero if and only if η restricts to zero on f(X).

CLD 15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.5: A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, for every compact F and ordinary open neighbourhood U of F, there is an ordinary smooth function equal to one near F with compact support contained in U.

CLD Theorem 15.7.1 and 15.7.2: A Hausdorff pure n-dimensional analytic space, equipped with its canonical calibration and analytic boundary, is a tropical space of level n; the induced tropical structure on an analytic domain agrees with that domain's own analytic structure.

CLD 12.4.1–2, 12.8.2, 5.4.4, and Proposition 14.1.12: On a Hausdorff analytic space of dimension at most n, a unit moment on a compact analytic domain has a compact finite polyhedral image of dimension at most n. Its compact chart is pleasant, its tropical polyhedron is the top-dimensional part of that image, and its supporting top-dimensional skeleton admits cell decompositions adapted to the moment's compact piecewise immersion.

CLD 4.5.1–2 and 14.3.2–5: Standard calibrations are strictly positive and G-locally constant. On a paralinéaire subset of an affine space they admit a cell decomposition with a constant positive volume vector on each top cell. The canonical calibration of a skeletal subset of a Hausdorff analytic space of dimension at most n, considered at level n, is standard and is compatible with restriction to analytic domains.

CLD 14.2.2 and 14.5.1–2: For a pleasant moment f on a level-n analytic space, its moment-image calibration is the direct image of the canonical skeletal calibration. On an adapted top cell D, it equals d_D τ_{D,*}|e_1∧⋯∧e_n|, where τ_D is the affine inverse of a torus projection injective on D and d_D is the sum of the positive constant finite-flat degrees on the skeletal cells above D. These degrees use the full finite fibre algebras, including their lengths.

CLD 5.8.3–5 and Proposition 5.10.1(c,d): Canonically calibrated forms define carrier measures by contraction on a supporting skeleton. For a pleasant chart f and a Borel coefficient (p,n)-form η, p∈{n−1,n}, the associated Borel measure is locally finite exactly when η restricted to the calibrated tropical polyhedron is locally integrable; then f_*((f^*η)_Rad)=⟨η,μ_Πf⟩_Rad. For p=n, integration satisfies the corresponding tropical integral formula, smooth top forms are finite on compact moment domains, and lower-dimensional cells carry no top measure.

CLD 5.7.2, 7.3.5, and Lemma 7.7.5: On a tropical space of level n, a locally integrable real multiplier h defines an integration current by compact ordinary top-form pairings, and d′d″[h]=0 is equivalent to ∫h(d′d″α)_Rad=0 for every compact ordinary (n−1,n−1)-form α. Every continuous finite real multiplier is locally integrable.

CLD Proposition 14.3.6 and Proposition 15.3.1: For a Hausdorff analytic space of dimension at most n considered at level n, a complete analytic extension L/K, and scalar projection π, canonical skeletal calibrations satisfy π_*μ_L=μ. For a tropical-Borel (n,n) G-form ω, π_*ω_{L,Bor}=ω_Bor; if ω is locally integrable, π_*ω_{L,Rad}=ω_Rad, with no extension-degree factor.

CLD Remark 14.4.3: If F/K is finite and Z is a Hausdorff F-analytic space of dimension at most n considered at level n, its restricted K-analytic space Z_0 has the same dimension and skeletal subsets; on each such subset the canonical calibrations satisfy μ_{Z_0}=[F:K]μ_Z.

CLD 15.4.1 and Proposition 15.4.3: Let f:Y→X be a morphism of level-n K-analytic spaces finite over the complement of a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n. For a locally integrable (p,n) G-form ω, p∈{n−1,n}, f^*ω is locally integrable and f_*((f^*ω)_Rad)=dc(f)ω_Rad. For an analytic isomorphism the calibrated degree is one.

CLD 13.3.1–3: For an analytic morphism f:Y→X and y isolated in its fibre over x, deg_y(f) is the dimension over H(x) of that fibre's full local Artinian algebra. Under any complete scalar extension L/K, with projections p:X_L→X and q:Y_L→Y, and every x_L over x, deg_y(f)=Σ_{z∈f_L⁻¹(x_L)∩q⁻¹(y)}deg_z(f_L).
